candidates.instruction: Structure introductory conceptual lessons into five distinct phases: (1) an intuitive hook, (2) essential prerequisites, (3) formal definition, (4) visual synthesis/demonstration, and (5) real-world application. For theorems, ensure prerequisites (e.g., independence) are reviewed immediately before the core definition.
Coordinate the color highlighting of technical keywords in the lecture text with the stroke/fill colors of corresponding mobjects to reduce cognitive mapping load for the learner.
Employ established pedagogical analogies (e.g., 'hilly landscape' for loss functions, 'sniffer dog' for Bayes) in the lecture script to provide an intuitive conceptual anchor for abstract algorithms.

Replace abstract placeholders with concrete numerical examples and step-by-step calculations (e.g., using integer values like 3^x=81) for iterative or operational concepts. Numerical walkthroughs are essential for técnico mastery and bridging theory to practice.
Synchronize the dimensionality of mathematical formulas with their visual representations (e.g., 1D sequence formulas must use 1D sequence visuals) to avoid conceptual dissonance.

Ensure logical closure in concluding synthesis sections by defining all terms and displaying intermediate formulas (e.g., integral steps for coefficients) that link prerequisites to the final result. No new terminology (e.g., 'directrix') should appear for the first time in the summary.
Consolidate triadic operations (e.g., powers, roots, logs) in a final synthesis using a single geometric frame (like a triangle) to emphasize their unified relationship.

situation.problem_text:
Topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space

Target audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

Section: section_1 — Introduction: Scalars vs. Vectors

Lecture lines:
Scalars hold only magnitude information.
Vectors describe both magnitude and direction.
Imagine a cat weighing five kilograms.
Its jumping velocity is a vector.
Vectors are arrows in our space.

Planned animations:
Show scalar 's' as a Dot (#FFD700).
Show vector 'v' as an Arrow (#00CED1).
Label s as 'Scalar' and v as 'Vector'.

Section: section_2 — Vector Representation and Components

Lecture lines:
We represent space using coordinates.
A vector splits into horizontal, vertical parts.
Moving three right, four up.
Vector is [3, 4] from origin.

Planned animations:
Draw Cartesian plane with grid lines (#333333).
Plot vector (a, b) as an Arrow from origin (#00CED1).
Label components 'a' and 'b' on axes.

Section: section_3 — Vector Addition: The Parallelogram Rule

Lecture lines:
Add vectors head-to-tail for sum.
Parallelogram rule shows the resultant path.
Boat speed plus river current vectors.

Planned animations:
Display vectors v and w as Arrows (#00CED1).
Slide w to the head of v.
Draw resultant vector v+w as an Arrow (#FF4500).

Section: section_4 — Scalar Multiplication and Scaling

Lecture lines:
Scalar multiplication scales vector length.
Positive scalars preserve original direction.
Double speed boosts length to 2v.

Planned animations:
Display vector v as an Arrow (#00CED1).
Multiply v by scalar c.
Show resulting vector c*v scaling length (#FFD700).

Section: section_5 — Conclusion: Why Vectors Matter

Lecture lines:
Vectors are fundamental in physics.
Modern software relies on vector math.
They mathematically describe all motion.

Planned animations:
Summarize v as a collection of components.
Highlight the flexibility of vectors in physics.
Show vector v moving in space (#00CED1).

candidates.instruction: For large or complex mobject groups (such as Axes with plots or VGroups), use place_in_area with a multi-cell span (e.g., 'B2' to 'E5') rather than place_at_grid to ensure centering and panel separation. For coordinate systems, group Axes and their curves/points into a single VGroup before applying the layout method to keep them spatially synchronized.

Use simple Manim primitives (Dot, Square) as fallbacks when asset references are named 'none' or 'placeholder' in the storyboard. Avoid introducing irrelevant default icons (e.g., a microphone) that break semantic context.
Proactively apply a scale factor (0.4-0.7) to large containers (Axes, NumberPlane) in dual-panel layouts to avoid overlap with text panels and titles.

Prefer dedicated grid-cell placement for general label alignment (e.g., Row B for a target in Row C). However, for objects requiring precise anchors (such as vector tips), group the mobject and label in a VGroup using .next_to() before applying layout transformations.

Reserve Row A and the top-most cells of Row B as empty visual buffers for the section title. Only utilize Row A if the primary title is anchored to the screen edge (UP) and mobjects are scaled (<= 0.7) to ensure proper vertical breathing room.

In dual-panel layouts, confine mobjects to columns 3-6 and maintain a clear 1-unit horizontal gutter (typically Column 2 or 'B') between the left lecture text and right-side visuals. Only utilize all columns if the coordinate system is explicitly centered (x >= 0.5) to avoid 'poor grid utilization'.

When applying animations to collections (lists like self.mobjects or Graph dictionaries), do not pass the collection directly to the animation constructor. Use the unpacking operator (*) for lists (e.g., FadeOut(*self.mobjects)) or wrap dictionary values in a VGroup (e.g., VGroup(*graph.vertices.values())) to avoid TypeErrors.
Distribute multiple distinct mobjects (e.g., vectors, lines) across unique grid cells rather than stacking them at the same coordinate to prevent occlusion and conceptual confusion.
Restrict scale factor of secondary emphasis mobjects (checkmarks, arrows) to 0.8-1.2. Excessive scaling disruptions visual hierarchy.
Do not use a non-existent 'HGroup' class in Manim. Use 'VGroup' and apply the '.arrange(RIGHT)' method to achieve horizontal alignment.
Place mobjects intended for direct comparison in adjacent grid cells (e.g., D3, D4) to minimize eye travel and facilitate identification of differences.
Coordinate the color highlighting of technical keywords in the lecture text with the stroke/fill colors of corresponding mobjects to reduce cognitive mapping load for the learner.
When the storyboard describes a specific mathematical refinement (e.g., sqrt(d_k) scaling), the on-screen MathTex must explicitly display that term to ground the visual action.

When using Python raw strings (r'...') for MathTex, use single backslashes for LaTeX commands (e.g., r'\frac'). Avoid double-escaping (r'\\frac'), as it can pass literal double backslashes to the compiler, potentially causing compilation failure.
Do not use non-existent 'Checkmark' class; use Tex(r'$\checkmark$') or SVGMobject to render checkmark symbols and avoid NameErrors.

Animate the mechanical relationships (the 'how' and 'why') described by active process verbs (e.g., 'slides', 'flips', 'updating') using dynamic transformations like morphing, continuous motion paths, or area expansion. Avoid using static reveals or simplistic highlights to represent mechanical operations.
Anchor announcement text (e.g., 'Pattern Broken!') within the same visual rows or columns as the primary data it describes to maintain layout cohesion.
Do not use .get_midpoint() on VGroups or DashedLines; use .get_center() instead. These collections lack continuous paths and will trigger a point_from_proportion exception.

Maintain consistent visual style, fidelity, and dimensionality across all sections. Do not mix disparate design languages (e.g., rudimentary line art, flat-design icons, and photorealistic raster images) or change animation density abruptly in the summary unless required for comparative demonstration.
Store target values for updaters or always_redraw in a ValueTracker. Passing primitive numeric types (float, int) inside lambdas causes an AttributeError during render.
Apply multiple inheritance (e.g., class SectionScene(TeachingScene, MovingCameraScene)) when combining custom layout helpers and camera frame manipulation to prevent AttributeErrors for camera.frame.

When creating MathTex mobjects, isolate variables intended for targeted animation (e.g., set_color, Indicate) into independent string arguments. Indexing in Manim MathTex is determined by the input strings; grouping symbols in one string prevents the selection of individual components for precise visual effects.

Do not nest Manim animation objects (e.g., Circumscribe, Flash, Indicate) inside introducer animations like FadeIn. Pass the animation object directly to self.play() to avoid a TypeError, as introducers require Mobject arguments, not other Animation instances.

Group the text-highlighting animation and the corresponding mobject animation within the same self.play() call. Sequential calls create a perceptual lag that disrupts the link between verbal and visual information.
Use MoveAlongPath with the relevant curve object rather than .animate.move_to for constrained physics demonstrations (e.g., bead on a wire) to ensure visual accuracy.
Instantiate 3D surfaces first, then apply color and opacity via .set_color() and .set_opacity(). Passing these as keyword arguments directly to axes.plot_surface() triggers a TypeError.
Synchronize numerical values in MathTex (e.g., matrix entries) with the geometric properties (e.g., vector direction) of corresponding mobjects to avoid severe cognitive dissonance.
Use hexadecimal strings (e.g., '#00FFFF') for all color specifications to prevent NameErrors, as named constants like 'CYAN' are not globally available in all environments.
Prefer .animate syntax over legacy ApplyMethod to align with modern Manim standards and reduce code complexity.
Replace continuous per-frame updaters and complex path tracking (TracedPath) with discrete .animate transformations for simple movements to prevent render timeouts in complex scenes.
Visualize non-Archimedean metrics (e.g., p-adic) using hierarchical models like nested disks or tree diagrams rather than linear number lines to accurately represent divisibility-based distance.
Visualize parallel attention heads using distinct colors or spatial offsets before convergence to communicate the parallel architecture intuitively.

Do not pass advanced styling arguments (e.g., 'dash_array', 'dash_length', 'opacity') directly into VMobject or plot_surface constructors. Instead, apply these properties using specialized methods (.set_color_by_gradient, .set_opacity) or wrap the mobject in a specific class (DashedVMobject) to avoid TypeErrors.

When visualizing physical interactions (splitting, reflection), represent all causal elements (source, object, recording medium) rather than only the resulting rays/waves to maintain script-to-visual grounding.
Do not use a non-existent 'Curve' class. Use 'ArcBetweenPoints' or 'CubicBezier' for trajectories.
In Manim, use the 'Annulus' class for circular shapes with holes; do not use 'Ring', as it is not a standard primitive and will trigger a NameError.

Adjust self.wait() durations to be proportional to the word count of the lecture lines (approx. 0.4 seconds per word) with a minimum of 2 seconds. In complex scenes with dense formulas, ensure the terminal wait is at least 7-10 seconds to avoid rapid pacing that hinders learner absorption.
Do not assign values to self.time; it is a reserved read-only property for the internal clock. Use alternative names (e.g., self.current_time) for custom state variables.

Strictly adhere to the provided signatures of custom base class methods (e.g., place_at_grid). Do not pass standard Manim kwargs (e.g., 'shift') or hallucinated convenience methods (e.g., 'add_label') suggested by review agents unless they are explicitly defined in the local implementation.

Topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space

Target audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

Section: section_1 — Introduction: Scalars vs. Vectors

Lecture lines:
Scalars hold only magnitude information.
Vectors describe both magnitude and direction.
Imagine a cat weighing five kilograms.
Its jumping velocity is a vector.
Vectors are arrows in our space.

Planned animations:
Show scalar 's' as a Dot (#FFD700) next to [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cat.png].
Show vector 'v' as an Arrow (#00CED1).
Label s as 'Scalar' and v as 'Vector'.

Current section code:
from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introduction: Scalars vs. Vectors", [
            "Scalars hold only magnitude information.",
            "Vectors describe both magnitude and direction.",
            "Imagine a cat weighing five kilograms.",
            "Its jumping velocity is a vector.",
            "Vectors are arrows in our space."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        s = Dot(color="#FFD700")
        s_label = Text("Scalar", font_size=20, color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(s, 'B2', scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(s_label, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(s), FadeIn(s_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#00CED1")
        v_label = Text("Vector", font_size=20, color="#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(v, 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(v), FadeIn(v_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00CED1")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Parallelogram Rule", [
            "Add vectors head-to-tail for sum.", 
            "Parallelogram rule shows the resultant path.", 
            "Boat speed plus river current vectors."
        ])
        
        # Vectors
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00CED1", buff=0)
        w = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color="#00CED1", buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex("v", color="#00CED1").next_to(v.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        w_label = MathTex("w", color="#00CED1").next_to(w.get_center(), LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        v_group = VGroup(v, v_label)
        w_group = VGroup(w, w_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.place_at_grid(v_group, 'C2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(w_group, 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(v_group), Create(w_group))
        
        # Slide w to head of v
        w_moved = w.copy()
        w_moved.shift(v.get_end() - w.get_start())
        w_moved_label = w_label.copy().next_to(w_moved.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(w.animate.shift(v.get_end()), w_label.animate.next_to(w_moved.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        resultant = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=v.get_end() + w.get_end(), color="#FF4500", buff=0)
        res_label = MathTex("v+w", color="#FF4500").next_to(resultant.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(resultant), Write(res_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        # No extra animation needed for the 3rd point as per prompt constraints
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: Why Vectors Matter", [
            "Vectors are fundamental in physics.", 
            "Modern software relies on vector math.", 
            "They mathematically describe all motion."
        ])
        
        # Define mobjects once
        v_arrow = Vector(UP * 1.5 + RIGHT * 1.5, color=WHITE)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=WHITE).next_to(v_arrow, UP)
        vector_group = VGroup(v_arrow, v_label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(vector_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(vector_group)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00CED1"))
        # Move vector to simulate motion
        self.play(vector_group.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1 + DOWN * 0.5), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication and Scaling", [
            "- Scalar multiplication scales vector length.",
            "- Positive scalars preserve original direction.",
            "- Double speed boosts length to 2v."
        ])
        
        # 1. Vector v setup (Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png)

        car.height = 0.6
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#00CED1", buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#00CED1", font_size=32)
        v_group = Group(car, v, v_label).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # 2. Vector 2v setup (Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg)
        speedometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg")
        speedometer.height = 0.6
        v_2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*3.0, color="#FFD700", buff=0)
        v_2_label = MathTex(r"2\vec{v}", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)

        self.play(FadeIn(v_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        self.play(ReplacementTransform(v_group, v_2_group))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication and Scaling", [
            "- Scalar multiplication scales vector length.",
            "- Positive scalars preserve original direction.",
            "- Double speed boosts length to 2v."
        ])
        
        # --- Create objects ---
        # 1. Vector v (Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png)
        car = ImageMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png")
        car.height = 0.5
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#00CED1", buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#00CED1", font_size=28)
        # Fix: VGroup cannot hold ImageMobject; use Group instead
        v_group = Group(car, v, v_label).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # 2. Vector 2v (Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg)
        speedometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg")
        speedometer.height = 0.5
        v_2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*3.0, color="#FFD700", buff=0)
        v_2_label = MathTex(r"2\vec{v}", color="#FFD700", font_size=28)
        v_2_group = Group(speedometer, v_2, v_2_label).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)

        # --- Animations ---
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(v_group, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(v_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.place_in_area(v_2_group, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(v_group, v_2_group))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication and Scaling", [
            "- Scalar multiplication scales vector length.",
            "- Positive scalars preserve original direction.",
            "- Double speed boosts length to 2v."
        ])
        
        # --- Create objects ---
        # 1. Vector v with Car
        car = ImageMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png")
        car.height = 0.6
        v = Arrow(start=LEFT*0.75, end=RIGHT*0.75, color="#00CED1", buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\\vec{v}", color="#00CED1", font_size=32)
        v_group = Group(car, v, v_label).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # 2. Vector 2v with Speedometer
        speedometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg")
        speedometer.height = 0.6
        v_2 = Arrow(start=LEFT*1.5, end=RIGHT*1.5, color="#FFD700", buff=0)
        v_2_label = MathTex(r"2\\vec{v}", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)
        v_2_group = Group(speedometer, v_2, v_2_label).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)

        # --- Animations ---

        self.place_in_area(v_group, 'B3', 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(v_group))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00CED1")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        self.play(ReplacementTransform(v_group, v_2_group))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

Coordinate the color highlighting of technical keywords in the lecture text with the stroke/fill colors of corresponding mobjects to reduce cognitive mapping load for the learner.
When the storyboard describes a specific mathematical refinement (e.g., sqrt(d_k) scaling), the on-screen MathTex must explicitly display that term to ground the visual action.

Do not pass advanced styling arguments (e.g., 'dash_array', 'dash_length', 'opacity') directly into VMobject or plot_surface constructors. Instead, apply these properties using specialized methods (.set_color_by_gradient, .set_opacity) or wrap the mobject in a specific class (DashedVMobject) to avoid TypeErrors.
Do not use a non-existent 'Curve' class. Use 'ArcBetweenPoints' or 'CubicBezier' for trajectories.

Adjust self.wait() durations to be proportional to the word count of the lecture lines (approx. 0.4 seconds per word) with a minimum of 2 seconds. In complex scenes with dense formulas, ensure the terminal wait is at least 7-10 seconds to avoid rapid pacing that hinders learner absorption.
In Manim, use the 'Annulus' class for circular shapes with holes; do not use 'Ring', as it is not a standard primitive and will trigger a NameError.
Do not assign values to self.time; it is a reserved read-only property for the internal clock. Use alternative names (e.g., self.current_time) for custom state variables.

Animate the mechanical relationships (the 'how' and 'why') described by active process verbs (e.g., 'slides', 'flips', 'updating') using dynamic transformations like morphing, continuous motion paths, or area expansion. Avoid using static reveals or simplistic highlights to represent mechanical operations.
Anchor announcement text (e.g., 'Pattern Broken!') within the same visual rows or columns as the primary data it describes to maintain layout cohesion.

Maintain consistent visual style, fidelity, and dimensionality across all sections. Do not mix disparate design languages (e.g., rudimentary line art, flat-design icons, and photorealistic raster images) or change animation density abruptly in the summary unless required for comparative demonstration.
Use MoveAlongPath with the relevant curve object rather than .animate.move_to for constrained physics demonstrations (e.g., bead on a wire) to ensure visual accuracy.
Visualize non-Archimedean metrics (e.g., p-adic) using hierarchical models like nested disks or tree diagrams rather than linear number lines to accurately represent divisibility-based distance.

When visualizing physical interactions (splitting, reflection), represent all causal elements (source, object, recording medium) rather than only the resulting rays/waves to maintain script-to-visual grounding.
Visualize parallel attention heads using distinct colors or spatial offsets before convergence to communicate the parallel architecture intuitively.
